title: Azure architecture cost trade-offs
description: Evaluate cost against performance, availability, and security when designing Azure architectures. Learn how reserved instances, savings plans, and service tiers affect total cost of ownership.

data.text: In the cloud, you trade money for speed, resilience, and convenience. A fully redundant, zone-aware, always-on architecture costs more than a single-instance backup-and-restore setup. The goal is not to minimize cost at all costs, but to find the right balance for each workload based on business value.

Azure billing includes compute charges, storage capacity and operations, data transfer, and service-specific fees. Many teams focus on compute because it is visible on the invoice, but data transfer and redundancy can add significant cost. For example, zone-redundant storage is more expensive than locally redundant storage, but it may eliminate the need for a separate backup region.

terms.definition: On-demand pricing with no upfront commitment. Highest per-unit cost, maximum flexibility.
One-year or three-year commitments for up to 72% savings compared to pay-as-you-go.
Flexible commitment to a specific spend amount per hour, applicable across eligible compute services.
Unused Azure compute sold at steep discounts, but evictable when Azure needs capacity back.

rows: Same SLA but survives zone failure
Near-100% availability if one region fails
Lowest RTO, but double the baseline cost

data.text: Start with the right service tier. Azure App Service has Dev, Basic, Standard, Premium, and Isolated tiers. A development workload does not need Premium. Use the Azure Pricing Calculator to estimate costs before committing, and use Azure Cost Management + BUDGETS to set alerts when spending exceeds expectations.

data.title: Cost Management budget alert in Bicep
data.content: Create a budget that triggers an alert when monthly spending exceeds a threshold.

data.title: Cost trade-off rules
items: Use pay-as-you-go for unpredictable or experimental workloads.
Use reserved instances for production databases and stable web tiers.
Use Spot VMs for fault-tolerant batch and CI/CD workloads.
Right-size VMs and App Service plans before scaling out.
Delete unused resources; enable auto-shutdown for dev environments.

data.title: Cost is a feature requirement
data.text: Treat cost as a non-functional requirement alongside latency and availability. Document cost targets in architecture reviews, just as you document SLAs. The most reliable architecture is worthless if it is unaffordable.

data.title: Key takeaways
points: Every reliability improvement has a cost; balance it against business value.
Reserved instances and savings plans reduce compute costs significantly.
Zone and multi-region redundancy increase both cost and availability.
Azure Cost Management with budgets turns spending from a surprise into a signal.
data.takeaway: The best Azure architecture is the one that is reliable enough at a cost the business can sustain.
